skill.name: agents-v2-py
skill.description: Build container-based Azure AI Foundry hosted agents with the Python Azure AI Projects SDK.
skill.summary: Guide Python developers through Azure AI Foundry hosted agent setup, configuration, versioning, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code spans, Python imports, placeholder URLs, and documented environment variable access. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious execution logic was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Example endpoints and image names could be mistaken for deployable values.
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholder URLs, MCP endpoints, and container images clearly, and tell users to use only trusted registries and services.

remediation.issue: Environment variable examples pass configuration into hosted containers.
remediation.suggestion: State that secrets should use managed identity or Azure Key Vault, and keep direct environment variables for non-secret configuration.

remediation.issue: The installation example uses a minimum version range.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact Azure SDK versions tested by the author, especially for beta releases.

content.value_statement: Container-hosted agents require specific SDK, identity, and registry setup. This skill guides Python creation, configuration, version management, and troubleshooting for Azure AI Foundry hosted agents.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure AI Projects SDK and Azure Identity packages.
Explains required Azure resources, ACR pull permissions, and capability host setup.
Provides Python examples for creating, listing, and deleting hosted agent versions.
Demonstrates ImageBasedHostedAgentDefinition with protocol versions, CPU, memory, tools, and image settings.
Covers code interpreter, file search, and MCP tool configuration examples.
Includes synchronous and asynchronous hosted agent creation patterns.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure AI Foundry project and Azure permissions.
Does not build or scan the container image for the user.
Uses example values that must be replaced with environment-specific settings.
Does not validate billing, quota, or regional availability for hosted agents.

use_cases.title: Create a Hosted Agent Prototype
use_cases.description: Set up a first Python hosted agent using a custom container image and Azure identity.

use_cases.title: Standardize Cloud Agent Deployment
use_cases.description: Document required registry permissions, capability host settings, and resource allocations for repeatable deployments.

use_cases.title: Debug Hosted Agent Configuration
use_cases.description: Review common errors related to image pulls, protocol versions, and missing capability hosts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hosted Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a basic Azure AI Foundry hosted agent in Python using my container image and project endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Agent Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to set CPU, memory, protocol version, and environment variables for a Python hosted agent.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tools to a Hosted Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure code interpreter, file search, and an MCP tool for an Azure AI hosted agent.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my hosted agent deployment plan for image versioning, permissions, resource sizing, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy a container-based Azure AI hosted agent from ACR.
output_examples.output: The response outlines prerequisites, identity setup, project endpoint configuration, hosted agent creation steps, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: My hosted agent fails with an image pull error.
output_examples.output: The response identifies likely registry permission issues and suggests checking image tags, ACR access, and managed identity role assignment.

output_examples.input: I want an asynchronous version of the hosted agent setup.
output_examples.output: The response describes the async client pattern, credential lifecycle, hosted agent creation flow, and where to add deployment-specific values.

best_practices: Use managed identity and DefaultAzureCredential for Azure authentication.
Use specific container image tags for production deployments.
Validate ACR permissions, capability host setup, and protocol versions before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode secrets in container environment variables.
Do not use untrusted container images or MCP endpoints.
Do not rely on latest image tags for production hosted agents.

faq.question: What Azure SDK version does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects azure-ai-projects version 2.0.0b3 or later for hosted agent support.

faq.question: Does this skill create the container image?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the image already exists in Azure Container Registry or another trusted registry.

faq.question: Which authentication method is recommended?
faq.answer: The examples recommend DefaultAzureCredential with Azure Identity.

faq.question: Can I configure agent tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows examples for code interpreter, file search, and MCP tools.

faq.question: Does this skill support asynchronous Python code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async pattern using aio credential and client classes.

faq.question: What should I check when deployment fails?
faq.answer: Check ACR pull permissions, image paths, capability host configuration, and protocol version settings.
